headline: Bipartisan legislative shifts and geopolitical flashpoints are creating a volatile trade environment where tariff relief is imminent but regional supply risks remain acute.

forces.b: A bipartisan push to restrict presidential tariff power has gained traction with three bills in Congress, while importers anticipate receiving $166 billion in universal refunds. Simultaneously, the EU and UK are delaying a 10% tariff on electric cars following industry pushback, and China-US liaison continues on reciprocal cuts.

Ocean freight rates remain elevated despite easing from near-record peaks, with port congestion now described as a 'new normal' in the US. The Black Sea has emerged as the world's deadliest shipping lane due to the Ukraine war, complicating global logistics.

While $166 billion in tariff refunds are expected to benefit US retail importers stocks, India has detained 85 containers of Scotch whisky and continues to hold Pernod Diageo shipments due to disputes. These friction points threaten specific regional inventory flows despite broader refund hopes.

The Ukraine war has turned the Black Sea into a high-risk zone, while Iran claims attacks on Omani islands aim to disrupt oil infrastructure. Additionally, Russia's African arms trade involving gold and guns adds another layer of geopolitical complexity.
